title: 5 Reasons Why Your Students Don't Like You
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin opens by dispelling the myth that holding students accountable makes them dislike a teacher, arguing that consistent follow-through actually strengthens likability and trust. He then lists five real causes of student dislike: going back on your word by stating rules and then applying them inconsistently; genuinely disliking students, which leaks out through micro-expressions no one can fully hide; letting students get under your skin and unconsciously seeking revenge through sarcasm; being chronically grumpy from outside stress that spills onto students; and being uptight, creating a tense classroom atmosphere that makes students anxious and jumpy. His overall formula for predictable likability boils down to two things — total reliance on a classroom management plan and consistent pleasantness — which he says together produce remarkable behavioral, academic, and personal outcomes for a teacher.
points: Holding students accountable is not the cause of dislike; inconsistent follow-through is.
Genuinely disliking students leaks out through micro-expressions, tone, and body language that students can read.
Letting students get under your skin triggers subtle, often subconscious, defensive sarcasm or rebuke.
A teacher's chronic stress or grumpiness spills onto students and decimates influence.
The likability formula reduces to two things: total reliance on a classroom management plan and consistent pleasantness.
quotes: Stating rules, policies, and/or procedures and then ignoring them or applying them inconsistently will cause students to dislike you intensely.
Your eyes. Your micro-expressions. Your tone and body language. It all exposes you for who you are and how you feel about your students.
It’s exceedingly hard to take disrespect or challenge on the chin day after day without returning the favor.
If you’re unprepared mentally, if you don’t take care of yourself and arrive at school unhappy, it will spill out onto your students.
1. 100% reliance on your classroom management plan. 2. Your consistent pleasantness.
